name: Hindi
where: Northern and central India; lingua franca across much of India
tagline: Learn Hindi and you can chat, joke and haggle across most of India, and follow Bollywood films and songs without subtitles.

name: Urdu
where: National language of Pakistan; official in several Indian states (Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, J&K and others); spoken by large diaspora communities in the UK, Gulf, USA and Canada
tagline: The language of ghazals, Bollywood lyrics and everyday Pakistan — and once you speak it, you can understand spoken Hindi too.

name: Bengali
where: Bangladesh (national language) and the Indian states of West Bengal, Tripura and parts of Assam (Barak Valley); large diaspora in the UK, Middle East and North America
tagline: The sweet, musical language of Tagore, Satyajit Ray and 280 million speakers, with almost no gender and very regular verbs.

name: Punjabi
speakers: ≈150 million (L1 + L2), across India, Pakistan and the diaspora
where: Punjab in India and Pakistan; large communities in the UK, Canada, the USA and Australia
tagline: A warm, musical, tonal language spoken by over a hundred million people — and the voice of bhangra, Sikh scripture and a worldwide diaspora.

name: Nepali
speakers: ≈19 million first-language speakers; ≈32 million including second-language speakers
where: Nepal (official language and lingua franca); Sikkim and the Darjeeling–Kalimpong hills of West Bengal, India (a scheduled language of India); southern Bhutan; Nepali communities in Assam, the Gulf, Malaysia, the UK, USA and Australia
tagline: Nepali opens up the Himalaya — from Kathmandu tea shops and trekking trails to Darjeeling and Sikkim — and Nepalis are delighted when a visitor makes the effort.

name: Pashto
where: Afghanistan (official language, alongside Dari) and Pakistan (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, northern Balochistan, the former tribal areas, and large communities in Karachi); diaspora in the Gulf, UK, Germany and North America
tagline: The proud, poetic language of the Pashtuns — learn it and every door in the mountains from Kandahar to Peshawar opens with a cup of green tea.

name: Sindhi
speakers: ≈32 million (L1), plus L2 speakers in Sindh
where: Sindh province of Pakistan (Karachi, Hyderabad, Sukkur, Larkana, Thar); in India among the Sindhi community (Kutch in Gujarat, Ulhasnagar and Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Delhi, Rajasthan); large diaspora in the Gulf, UK, USA, Hong Kong, Singapore and elsewhere
tagline: Learn the language of the Indus — of Shah Abdul Latif's poetry, ajrak and Sufi music — with sounds you will not hear in any other major South Asian language.

name: Marathi
where: Maharashtra (Mumbai, Pune, Nagpur), Goa, and Marathi communities across India and abroad
tagline: The language of Mumbai, Pune and Maharashtra — a thousand-year literary tradition, and the key to everyday life in India's richest state.

name: Gujarati
where: Gujarat (India), Daman & Diu, Dadra & Nagar Haveli, Mumbai; diaspora in the UK, East Africa, North America and the Gulf
tagline: The warm, quick-witted language of Gujarat's traders, poets and kitchens — and of Gandhi — spoken from Ahmedabad to Leicester to Nairobi.

name: Tamil
where: Tamil Nadu and Puducherry (India), northern and eastern Sri Lanka, Singapore (official language), Malaysia, and a large worldwide diaspora
tagline: One of the world's oldest living classical languages — over 2,000 years of literature — and still the everyday voice of tens of millions, from Chennai street stalls to Kollywood films.

name: Telugu
where: Andhra Pradesh and Telangana (India), with large communities in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Odisha and the diaspora (USA, Gulf, UK)
tagline: The most widely spoken Dravidian language, with a melodious, vowel-final sound and a booming film and tech culture.

name: Kannada
speakers: ≈44 million L1; ≈60 million including L2 speakers
where: Karnataka (south-western India) and neighbouring border districts of Maharashtra, Goa, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana; large diaspora in the Gulf, USA and UK
tagline: The language of Bengaluru, Mysuru and over a thousand years of literature, with one of the most logical, beautiful scripts in India.

name: Malayalam
where: Kerala and Lakshadweep (India), and large diaspora communities in the Gulf states, Singapore, Malaysia, the UK and North America
tagline: The rolling, musical language of Kerala: famous for its ഴ, its long words, and one of the most literate societies in the world.

name: Odia
where: Odisha (official language), plus neighbouring parts of Jharkhand, West Bengal, Chhattisgarh and Andhra Pradesh
tagline: A classical language with a beautifully rounded script, gentle sounds and no grammatical gender — the key to Odisha's temples, coast and kitchens.
